---
title: "Estimation of Location Names"
subtitle: "Estimation of location names from geographic coordinates"
---

## Overview

A common challenge in oceanographic datasets is missing or inconsistent location metadata. While sediment data usually come with coordinates (latitude and longitude), fields such as the **Nearest Country** and the **Nearest Municipality** are often left blank or recorded inconsistently.

To ensure consistency across the dataset, these fields are estimated from the station position. This page outlines the data sources and geospatial methods used to populate the `est_country`, `country_code`, `municipality` and `sea_name` columns in the [station](db-schema.qmd#station) table.

All four are produced by [seastamp](https://github.com/AIQC-Hub/seastamp), the command line tool that annotates locations for every stage of the pipeline, so the pilot values agree with the ones the later generations carry.

::: {.callout-note}
### Note on Accuracy
These values are **algorithmic estimates** based on geometric proximity. They may differ from the original survey records or from specific political definitions of maritime borders.
:::

## Nearest Country

Since sediment samples are taken underwater, they do not technically belong "inside" a country's land border. To identify the associated nation, a **nearest neighbour** search is used: the distance from the station position to every surrounding country polygon is measured, and the closest one wins.

*   **Data source:** **Natural Earth** 1:10m Admin 0 Countries, the most detailed of the three Natural Earth scales.
*   **Columns:** `est_country` holds the country name, `country_code` its **ISO 3166-1 alpha-3** code (`BEL` for Belgium).

Every station in this dataset is nearest to Belgium, which is what you would expect of four decades of Belgian marine monitoring.

## Nearest Municipality

For higher-resolution analysis, identifying the country is not enough, so the **nearest municipality** (Local Administrative Unit) is estimated the same way. This needs far more detailed geometry, since it has to include islands and complex coastal administrative borders.

*   **Data source:** the **Eurostat GISCO** LAU 2021 dataset, which gives official administrative boundaries for European countries down to municipality level.
*   **Coverage:** Europe only, which covers every station here.

## Sea and Ocean Names

To determine which body of water a sample was taken from, the position is matched against the official sea boundaries: a **point in polygon** test, falling back to the nearest polygon where a position sits slightly inland.

*   **Data source:** the **International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) Sea Areas v3**, the globally accepted standard for the limits of oceans and seas.

## Projection

The three nearest-neighbour and point-in-polygon searches all run in a **Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area** projection centred on the data, with the extent derived from the sampling points themselves. Coordinates are rounded to three decimal places and de-duplicated first, so stations repeated at one position are looked up once.

## Summary of Data Sources

| Field | Estimation Method | Data Source | seastamp command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nearest Country** | Nearest neighbour | Natural Earth 1:10m Admin 0 | `place` |
| **Country Code** | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 | Natural Earth 1:10m Admin 0 | `place` |
| **Municipality** | Nearest neighbour | Eurostat GISCO LAU 2021 | `place` |
| **Sea Name** | Point in polygon | IHO Sea Areas v3 | `sea` |

## What changed at v0.1.8

These columns were previously estimated in R with `sf`, `rnaturalearth` and `giscoR`. Moving to seastamp changed three of them across the 160 distinct station positions:

| Column | Change |
| :--- | :--- |
| `est_country` | unchanged, every station is nearest to Belgium |
| `country_code` | every row: the codes are now ISO alpha-3 (`BEL`) rather than alpha-2 (`BE`) |
| `municipality` | 129 of 160 positions (81%) reassigned |
| `sea_name` | every station |

The sea name is a single, clean correction. Every station previously read `North Atlantic Ocean`, which is true only in the sense that the North Sea drains into it. They now all read **`North Sea`**, which is where the samples were taken: the Belgian Continental Shelf lies entirely within it.
